claims.text: Transition-metal catalyst activity is governed by synergistic effects of catalyst composition and structure.
Transition-metal catalyst selectivity is governed by synergistic effects of catalyst composition and structure.
Transition-metal catalyst durability is governed by synergistic effects of catalyst composition and structure.
High-entropy alloys are composed of multiple elements in near-equiatomic proportions.
Systematically varying catalyst composition or nanostructure is proposed to isolate the effect of a specific property on catalytic performance.
The high-entropy effect modulates catalyst electronic structure and adsorption properties.
Lattice distortion in high-entropy alloys influences electronic structure and adsorption properties.
The sluggish-diffusion effect influences catalyst electronic structure and adsorption properties.
Composition-induced electronic-structure modulation changes adsorbate interactions and thereby enhances catalytic activity.
Composition-induced modulation of electronic structure and adsorption enhances catalytic selectivity.
Composition-induced modulation of electronic structure and adsorption enhances catalyst durability.
Optimized high-entropy-alloy catalysts will have greater catalytic activity than conventional Pt-based baselines.
Optimized high-entropy-alloy catalysts will have greater selectivity than conventional Pt-based baselines.
Optimized high-entropy-alloy catalysts will have greater durability than conventional Pt-based baselines.
Tuning high-entropy alloys into nanostructures can improve catalytic performance.
The hypothesis is intended to hold only within an unspecified range of operating conditions and catalyst compositions or structures that permits observable synergistic effects.
The exact relationship between catalyst composition or structure and catalytic performance remains incompletely understood.
Failure of composition or structure optimization, including use of high-entropy alloys or nanostructures, to improve catalytic performance would falsify the hypothesis.
